observationsNotFindings: This is the first artifact in the catalog family to lean on a pin that is both dual-reviewed and recorded. The language-quality-leftover-join v2 carries Claude ACCEPT 0/0, Codex ACCEPT 0/0 and D-165, and I verified all three limbs. It is a noticeably firmer footing than the single-reviewer chains under DR-112 and DR-122, and worth the coordinator registering as a contrast.

The register row here is SATISFIED, which makes this catalog the one most exposed to accidental reopening, and it handles that well. It asserts no file 08 token, states the non-reopening twice, and confines itself to naming corpus classes for the DR-G14 qualification that DR-119's own row routes closure evidence to. The SATISFIED standing and the remaining qualification work are separate things and the artifact keeps them separate.

The quoted class text does its own boundary work, as in the G18 catalog. offline-signed-closure excludes G06 authoritative product offline and DR-106; hostile-substitutions excludes G07 verified-tree loader replacement and G22 platform-TCB resolution; clean-matrix restricts cells to TypeScript only and declares Windows is not a cell. Those exclusions are inherited from live G14 v1 rather than authored here.

Three DR-118 leftovers - OBL-THRESHOLDS, OBL-MATRIX-CORPUS, OBL-G13-RESERVED - remain open in the recorded join, and G13 stays reserved. A reader might expect a G14 corpus catalog to touch language-quality thresholds; it does not, and the separation is stated on both sides.

decision.summaryForCoordinator: No blockers, no should-fix. Every quotation is exact: namedCorpusNotAuthored equals live G14 v1 element-wise, and all three classes reproduce memberVerbatim, exactByteIntent and passProperty byte-for-byte - nine comparisons, all passing - with class ids clean-matrix, offline-signed-closure and hostile-substitutions reproduced from live ids in order rather than minted. The numeric-threshold prohibition I tested by sweeping for values: all nine threshold mentions are denials or DR-118 obligation names, and the only bare integers are 0, 1, 26 and the 02 and 08 path segments. The reopening risk is the distinctive one here, since DR-119 is SATISFIED under D-056 Class B via D-091; the catalog asserts no file 08 token at all, states the non-reopening twice, and confines itself to the DR-G14 qualification that DR-119's own row routes closure evidence to. The three DR-118 leftovers are named only to be refused, and I confirmed all three are still open in the recorded join. One pin claims more than any other in this family - 'Claude ACCEPT 0/0; Codex ACCEPT 0/0; recorded D-165' - and all three limbs verify: both verdicts exist at 0/0 and live COORD carries D-165 recording that join. That makes this the firmest evidence base of any catalog in the sweep, and neither pin is mine, so nothing here is self-corroborating. 19 attacks run, 19 refuted.
